description:
The Carbon Accountant collects, manages and analyses emissions data to determine an organisation’s carbon emissions footprints. He/She is involved in quantifying emissions, preparing compliance reports in adherence to relevant environmental regulations and reporting standards. He also leads efforts to upgrade emission data infrastructure and internal data collection processes, ensuring consistency of data measurement techniques, to contribute to an organisation’s sustainability and climate change mitigation goals. 

The Carbon Accountant requires strong analytical and communication skills, as well as attention to detail. He requires industry-leading knowledge and expertise in carbon accounting methodologies, emissions reporting standards, regulatory frameworks and data governance.
performance_expectation:
- Certified Public Accountant (CPA) from Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants (ISCA)
- Certified Sustainability Reporting Specialist (CSRS) 
- Certified Carbon Reporting Specialist (CCRS)
- Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) Certification

cwf.critical_work_function:
Conduct emissions data collection and 
calculations to inform carbon accounting and 
reporting
key_tasks: Maintain accurate emissions inventory for an organisation by managing inventory processes and reporting cycles
Analyse collected emission data from different scopes, applying the relevant factors to calculate an organisation’s carbon footprint, and identify trends and potential areas for emissions reduction
Implement Life Cycle Analysis and other relevant frameworks to assess an organisation’s environmental impact as a result of its products, processes or services
Conduct sector-specific research to inform the development of customised tools, emissions factors and data assets to increase the accuracy of carbon accounting
Lead the development and implementation of an organisation’s greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting processes
Establish baseline emissions and develop methodologies and procedures to facilitate ongoing tracking and monitoring of an organisation’s emissions
Implement carbon accounting and calculations software, tools and methodologies to facilitate data calculation and reporting for emissions inventory development

cwf.critical_work_function:
Ensure that an organisation’s carbon reporting processes, accounting reports, and monitoring systems adhere to reporting frameworks, 
regulations and methodologies
key_tasks: Prepare carbon reports in compliance with current and emerging national and international reporting standards and regulations, detailing emissions categorised by scope, emissions hotspots, and potential areas for emissions reduction
Facilitate the data verification process of collected emissions data and the organisation’s emissions reports, by working with external auditors and third-party verifiers to validate emissions data
Align an organisation’s internal data collection and control requirements with current and emerging regulatory assurance requirements
Establish robust monitoring systems for tracking and adjusting emissions inventories as new activities arise for early detection of non-compliance and mitigate risks
Strengthen internal controls and processes to ensure the integrity and traceability of emissions data and resolve audit discrepancies
Maintain detailed records of carbon accounting methodologies, assumptions and changes in data collection processes for transparent reporting and data consistency

cwf.critical_work_function:
Recommend carbon mitigation strategies and 
opportunities to organisations
key_tasks: Recommend measures and mitigation options to reduce an organisation’s emissions
Advise on adjustments to emissions reduction targets, based on organisation’s carbon and sustainability goals

cwf.critical_work_function:
Recommend robust emission data 
infrastructure and data strategies for improving data quality, accuracy, and consistency in 
carbon accounting
key_tasks: Improve carbon accounting methodologies by referencing best practices for carbon accounting informed by emerging industry standards, approaches and regulations
Propose upgrading for an organisation’s data infrastructure for easier identification of key carbon footprint emission factors
Review GHG emissions inventories for quality assurance and quality control, cross-checking emissions data from various sources to ensure accuracy and consistency
Standardise data collection protocols across various emissions categories for consistency and comparability

description:
The Decarbonisation Consultant provides advisory services to organisations on the development and implementation of sustainable practices, with the aim of reducing carbon footprints and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. He/She advises organisations on carbon mitigation strategies and sustainability reporting. He stays abreast of industry trends, regulatory changes and frameworks related to carbon mitigation and decarbonisation. In addition, he is adept at navigating key sustainability and carbon mitigation pathways, conducting feasibility and needs assessments, developing tailored sustainability plans and advising on the implementation of carbon mitigation projects and initiatives.

As a subject matter expert in carbon mitigation and offsetting strategies, the Decarbonisation Consultant requires a deep understanding of relevant regulations, best practices and frameworks. He also possesses business acumen, strategic thinking, analytical and problem-solving abilities to address sustainability challenges, as well as strong communication skills to engage different stakeholder types for the collective attainment of sustainability goals.

cwf.critical_work_function:
Develop strategies and implementation plans 
to facilitate organisations’ carbon mitigation 
journeys
key_tasks: Interpret relevant international, national and industry-specific regulations and frameworks related to decarbonisation, to advise on voluntary best practices and/or compliance requirements related to carbon mitigation strategies

Advise on emissions reduction target setting, based on organisation’s carbon footprint and its sustainability goals, and recommend measures and mitigation options to reduce an organisation’s emissions

Develop carbon mitigation strategies and plans for reducing emissions through various levers and multi-pronged approaches, setting clear objectives and milestones that will result in the attainment of emissions targets

Forecast future emissions trajectories resulting from carbon mitigation projects and initiatives, providing quantitative assessments of the various emissions scenarios and outcomes that could be attained
Recommend appropriate metrics to track implementation progress and performance in order to identify areas for continuous improvement

Oversee the implementation of recommended carbon mitigation and decarbonisation measures, working closely with stakeholders to obtain buy-in and cooperation, and managing project timelines, resources and risks

Review emissions reductions achieved from decarbonisation and carbon mitigation initiatives to provide analysis on the environmental and financial cost-savings of carbon mitigation initiatives, evaluating impact on business performance
Monitor emerging trends, best practices and new carbon market conditions or regulatory changes related to carbon mitigation, to advise on opportunities for improving carbon mitigation initiatives

cwf.critical_work_function: Engage various stakeholders to garner support for carbon mitigation strategies and sustainable change
key_tasks: Identify key stakeholders that need to be actively engaged to ensure the success of carbon mitigation projects or initiatives
Engage multiple, varied stakeholders involved in a carbon mitigation projects or initiatives, building consensus and driving collective action towards sustainability goals
Assess the interests and concerns of different stakeholders to ensure that the outcomes of carbon mitigation projects or initiatives are inclusive, equitable and sustainable

cwf.critical_work_function:
Explore opportunities for carbon offsetting for 
emissions that cannot be reduced directly
key_tasks: Conduct market research on carbon prices, demands, mechanisms and trading opportunities in both compliance and voluntary markets
Assess the viability and potential benefits of participation in carbon trading and offsetting opportunities, estimating the potential emissions reductions
Evaluate carbon offset options and their environmental and social benefits, to identify suitable projects that align with the sustainability goals of organisations

Propose carbon mitigation opportunities for the organisation based on the carbon mitigation hierarchy, including offsetting options for emissions that are hard to abate, and providing guidance on how to choose appropriate carbon credits

cwf.critical_work_function:
Perform needs assessment for organisations 
by evaluating carbon footprints and 
decarbonisation goals
key_tasks: Engage with internal and external stakeholders to understand overall sustainability goals, carbon reduction targets, compliance requirements and expectations related to carbon mitigation strategies
Gather data on organisation’s energy uses, emissions sources and other relevant data points, as well as carbon accounting outcomes, to understand organisation’s carbon footprint

Consolidate key trends from industry benchmarks and external data sources that are relevant to consultancy scope, to understand how organisation compares against similar industry players in terms of decarbonisation efforts and outcomes
Analyse how current carbon regulations and policies affect organisation’s operations and financials

Conduct gap analyses for organisation’s current state by assessing their carbon footprint and sustainability practices against established emissions reduction targets, relevant regulatory requirements and industry benchmarks and best practices in decarbonisation

description:
The Carbon Project Developer is responsible for the development and implementation of carbon projects, from conception to implementation and credit issuance. He/She conducts market research and examines potential areas for emissions removal, reduction or storage for carbon project development. He creates and monitors project plans, ensuring projects comply with relevant methodologies and requirements, and liaises with validation and verification bodies (VVBs) for the validation and verification of carbon projects. He will also work alongside various stakeholders, including local communities, regulatory bodies and traders, throughout the project duration to ensure the smooth implementation of the project, and eventual carbon credit issuance.

The Carbon Project Developer requires strong analytical and project management skills, as well as business acumen to understand the context and requirements of organisations. As a project developer, he must possess strong time management and stakeholder management capabilities, and demonstrate knowledge of carbon accounting methodologies, project management frameworks, digital technologies used for carbon projects, as well as international, national and industry regulations and policies related to carbon markets.

cwf.critical_work_function:
Design and develop carbon project plans as 
per the Project Design Document (PDD), 
ensuring compliance with standards, 
regulations and policies, and conduct feasibility studies to evaluate impacts of solutions and 
technologies
key_tasks: Support the planning, content development and technical writing for the Project Design Document (PDD) and overall project certification
Select suitable carbon standards and the associated carbon accounting methodologies based on project type, to guide project design and approach and ensure alignment to the standard
Prepare project plans, project profitability and cash flow, resourcing plans, and overall timelines for carbon projects, demonstrating project feasibility
Identify potential project risks, in order to develop mitigation plans to ensure project success and minimise negative impacts
Assess the potential social and environmental co-benefits of carbon projects, in order to enhance value of carbon credits or obtain additional project funding
Evaluate the impacts of integrating technology-based solutions as part of carbon projects, assessing their implications on emissions reduction, communities and carbon credit value
Create monitoring and reporting plans and frameworks to track project emission reductions, removals, progress and impact, in alignment with verification requirements and emissions reduction goals
Liaise with rating agencies to evaluate project feasibility, financial viability, project risks and alignment to regulation and carbon standards

cwf.critical_work_function:
Identify and liaise with local stakeholders, 
organising discussions to align on project 
objectives, community interests and education, and project revenue sharing
key_tasks: Conduct stakeholder analysis to identify key local bodies, community leaders, and organisations relevant to the carbon project

Work with local communities, governments, and other relevant stakeholders through consultations and feedback sessions to understand community interests, and ensure project alignment, social and environmental acceptability
Foster partnerships with key stakeholders, including project owners, investors, rating agencies, and carbon credit buyers, to ensure carbon project buy-in and financial support
Create educational materials and organise workshops on the benefits of carbon projects to raise awareness of carbon credits and sustainability practices
Launch campaigns focused on promoting sustainable practices, and the importance and impacts of carbon projects within the community
Facilitate the equitable sharing of carbon credit revenues with local communities by liaising with local stakeholders and regulators to promote transparency and community engagement

cwf.critical_work_function:
Identify carbon project opportunities through 
market research, emissions analysis and 
pre-feasibility studies
key_tasks: Conduct market research and analysis into carbon project types, standards and methodologies, and regulatory changes, to identify potential opportunities for carbon project development
Analyse organisational activities, processes and emissions data to identify potential focus areas for future carbon projects
Keep abreast of changes to policies, standards, and best practices in carbon markets, and carbon projects by monitoring evolving compliance and voluntary markets and related governmental frameworks
Collect, quantify and analyse emissions data to establish baselines for carbon projects, referencing emissions data from carbon projects
Support the evidencing of additionality for carbon projects through additionality assessments and carbon accounting methodologies
Explore potential public and private funding options, financial mechanisms and carbon credit revenue streams to support project implementation

cwf.critical_work_function:
Implement and execute carbon projects, 
tracking project progress against 
pre-determined timelines and project plans
key_tasks: Coordinate with internal teams and external partners to facilitate carbon project implementation efficiently as per project timelines

Implement monitoring plans to regularly track carbon project progress, ensuring project stays on track to achieve emissions reduction targets whilst adhering to relevant methodologies and requirements
Highlight potential discrepancies that arise from project monitoring, conducting reviews to investigate and troubleshoot technical issues
Conduct site visits at carbon project locations to complete quality assurance checks and technical reviews

cwf.critical_work_function:
Support in the monitoring, reporting and 
verification processes of carbon projects to 
enable carbon credit issuance
key_tasks: Collect and review emissions reduction data using tools such as remote sensing technologies, in accordance with appropriate carbon standard methodologies to show evidence of project activities
Prepare carbon project for validation and verification reviews
Prepare and review progress reports and other documentation required for internal and external stakeholders in compliance with regulations, policies and standards

Liaise and negotiate with validation and verification bodies (VVBs) to drive the validation and verification of carbon projects, ensuring the timely registration of the carbon project for carbon credit issuance
Ensure carbon credit issuance for completed projects through monitoring, reporting and verification processes and frameworks

description:
The Carbon Investment Specialist is responsible for conducting comprehensive market research and analysis into carbon markets 
and organisational carbon emissions data to identify potential, financially viable carbon investment opportunities. He/She performs 
feasibility studies and assesses the financial and environmental implications of selected carbon projects, identifying risks while also 
ensuring compliance with regulatory policies. He will also be in charge of monitoring the overall portfolio of carbon projects and tracks portfolio performance and forecasts investment returns and potential risks as part of findings to investors and traders. 

The Carbon Investment Specialist requires strong analytical and time management skills, attention to detail, as well as business 
acumen, in order to understand the organisation’s context and requirements. As an advisor to organisations, he must possess strong 
financial acumen and demonstrate knowledge of financial analysis and carbon accounting methodologies, as well as international, 
national and industry regulations and policies related to the carbon market.

cwf.critical_work_function:
Assess the financial viability and potential 
returns of identified carbon projects
key_tasks: Calculate the value of carbon credits that projects can generate using pricing data from carbon markets, and estimate potential emissions reductions
Evaluate additional environmental or social benefits generated by carbon projects which could increase the value of carbon credits
Develop financial models that forecast the future cash flows of projects, considering carbon credit revenue, operational costs, and capital investments
Conduct stress tests to simulate project performance under different scenarios, analysing the sensitivity to fluctuations in carbon prices and regulatory changes
Execute carbon investments and assist in the purchase of carbon credits, ensuring all regulatory, financial and operational requirements are met

cwf.critical_work_function:
Conduct carbon project due diligence, 
assessing their environmental impacts and 
compliance with legal and regulatory 
requirements
key_tasks: Ensure carbon projects meets sustainability, legal and regulatory standards, conducting due diligence in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, including project developers, internal operational managers and legal specialists
Conduct thorough risk assessments to ensure that carbon investments are viable and aligned with the risk tolerance levels and sustainability goals
Conduct detailed reviews of the carbon project technical documentation, including expected emission reductions, financial costs developments and compliance to regulatory requirements
Evaluate whether carbon projects can generate carbon credits under existing regulatory or voluntary market schemes

cwf.critical_work_function:
Develop and formalise carbon investment 
structures that balance the interests of all 
stakeholders involved
key_tasks: Negotiate carbon credit purchase agreements to secure carbon credits from specific projects
Design the financial structure of carbon project-related deals to provide capital for carbon project developers, ensuring that terms are favourable for the stakeholders involved

cwf.critical_work_function:
Recommend potential carbon investment 
opportunities suitable for the organisation 
based on information from various sources
key_tasks: Collaborate with stakeholders to understand potential impacts of regulatory changes on compliance and voluntary carbon markets

Synthesise information from various sources including market research to gain insights related to international and national carbon markets, supply and demand, and identify potential project opportunities across carbon market segments
Provide carbon investment recommendations based on research findings to portfolio managers and traders, highlighting the strategic fit and financial benefits of the investment
Prepare written analyses, evaluations and presentations on potential investment opportunities for review by relevant stakeholders
Stay abreast of global sustainability trends, emerging carbon reduction and removal technologies, competitor landscapes, and best practices in sustainable investments
Analyse pricing, liquidity and transaction data to identify carbon market trends and pricing drivers
Create reports and updates on types of carbon credit projects, carbon market research findings and carbon pricing trends for relevant stakeholders
Monitor international, national and industry regulations and policies to carbon markets, keeping up to date with changes and potential impact on investment decisions

cwf.critical_work_function:
Work with other stakeholders, such as project 
development teams, to monitor carbon portfolio returns and environmental impact of carbon 
projects
key_tasks: Monitor the financial and environmental performance of ongoing investments against predetermined sustainability and financial metrics
Support the tracking of carbon investment pipeline and pace of project deployment for organisations
Track the performance of multiple projects in a portfolio, adjusting carbon investment allocation to optimise financial returns and reduce risks
Escalate issues with project and portfolio performance to relevant stakeholders as necessary
Prepare investment reports that summarise carbon project status, performance metrics, and compliance with environmental regulations
Support the development of divestment or reinvestment strategies based on long-term financial and sustainability goals, to ensure investments remain profitable over time
Recommend exit opportunities to optimise carbon portfolio returns, determining the right time to sell carbon credits or exit from carbon projects

description:
The Carbon Trader is responsible for negotiating and closing carbon credit transactions with both buyers and sellers. He/She monitors and analyses the carbon market for potential trading opportunities and new buyers and sellers, with the aim of building and managing carbon portfolios for organisations. He evaluates the opportunities to ensure validation, verification and accreditation of estimated and actual generated carbon credits. Using these carbon credits, he designs and implements deal structures that optimise returns for the involved parties, ensuring risks are mitigated and transaction follows trading regulations. 

The Carbon Trader requires strong analytical and time management skills, attention to detail as well as business acumen, to understand the various requirements of the carbon credit buyers and sellers. As an advisor to organisations, he must possess strong communication and negotiation skills, demonstrate knowledge of carbon pricing mechanisms, understand international, national, and industry regulations and policies related to the carbon market, while exhibiting adaptability to navigate the evolving landscape of carbon markets and adjust strategies as necessary.

description:
The Carbon Auditor is an external role that provides third-party assurance to organisations regarding their overall carbon footprint. He/She conducts assessments and validation of an organisation’s overall carbon footprint in compliance with current and emerging standards and regulations. He collects data from various emissions sources, taking into account the jurisdictions that the organisation operates in, to calculate the organisation’s carbon footprint, analysing data to ensure its accuracy and consistency. Through this, the Carbon Auditor identifies processes and activities with high emissions and reporting gaps, providing actionable recommendations for emissions reduction and improved compliance. He conducts on-site assessments where necessary and prepares detailed findings and documentation to communicate corrective actions that may be undertaken by the organisation and its carbon reporting team, to improve emissions reporting transparency and achieve its sustainability goals. 

The Carbon Auditor requires strong analytical and planning skills, attention to detail, as well as business acumen. As an advisor to organisations, he should possess industry-leading knowledge of auditing processes and compliance requirements related to various standards, and strong understanding of climate and sustainability issues across sectors and jurisdictions.

Compare carbon footprint metrics with industry benchmarks to validate results and highlight discrepancies
Ensure the emission factors used for calculations are accurate, up-to-date, and tailored to operational specifications, to strengthen quality and robustness of carbon footprint analysis

description:
The Carbon Verifier conducts assessments and validation of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions data for individual carbon projects. He/She prepares a verification plan to ensure that the design, planned monitoring procedures and carbon accounting of each carbon project is accurate, reliable and prepared in accordance with standards used by accreditation bodies. Following this, he conducts periodic verification to ensure that the project is implemented and operating as planned and meeting all applicable criteria, with emissions data being monitored and quantified accurately. He prepares reports documenting the findings from the verification process and issues an official verification statement to confirm that projects achieve its claimed emissions reduction or removals.

The Carbon Verifier requires strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, as well as business acumen. With industry-leading knowledge of certification bodies and accreditation requirements, he oversees the verification and validation process from an independent, third-party perspective, and effectively communicates complex concepts to various stakeholders.
performance_expectation:
Global Carbon Standards, such as:
-	Verified Emission Reduction Approach (VERA)
-	Gold Standard for the Global Goals
-	Compliance requirements (EU, ETS, Paris Agreement Article 6):
-	Voluntary Standards
-	ISCC CORSIA PLUS

cwf.critical_work_function: Advise on verification processes, document verification findings and submit official verification statements to secure carbon credits for carbon offset efforts
key_tasks: Advise project developers and other involved stakeholders on verification processes, data collection approaches, emission calculation methodologies and reporting procedures to an organisation, based on national, regional and international verification standards
Assess if an organisation undergoing verification has achieved the claimed emissions reductions or removals, and if carbon projects have met carbon reporting standards
Assess uncertainties and materiality thresholds to identify elements of the data that may be imprecise or variable, affecting the data’s accuracy
Highlight discrepancies and areas of non-conformance for an organisation undergoing verification to address and ensure adherence to verification frameworks
Share draft reports with audited organisation for inputs and discussions on corrective actions, including recommendations for improving verification for future cycles
Advise the project team to conduct an internal review of the draft report, ensuring alignment on verification findings with the organisation before the official report is released

Issue final verification reports and statements to the organisation, documenting verification findings and conclusions and acknowledging the project’s adherence to carbon standards if it fulfils all requirements
Submit the verification statement to the relevant accreditation bodies and follow up on the verification process, assisting with queries

cwf.critical_work_function: Conduct verification activities by evaluating carbon project parameters, methodologies and data sources
key_tasks: Identify sites related to project operations, outlining specific areas of investigation based on the PDD
Conduct on-site visits to collect primary data to assess monitoring techniques, verify data accuracy and identify potential discrepancies through data analysis and evaluation
Liaise with project developers to identify and engage appropriate interviewees involved in carbon projects, as part of data gathering, and corroboration of evidence detailed in PDD
Conduct data reliability assessments and sampling tests to evaluate the reliability of the data used to develop emissions inventories
Perform independent emissions calculations to cross-check, validate and verify the accuracy of calculation methodologies performed by the organisation conducting the project
Validate the accuracy and reliability of data sources used in emission estimation calculations, referencing project documentation, additional evidence or observations from site visits
Assess the suitability of methodologies for projects, carbon accounting procedures, and sustainability frameworks used in carbon reporting, ensuring compliance with carbon standards

Verify the additionality of projects by checking the additionality tests that have been applied for the project, and reviewing the project’s environmental and social impacts for co-benefit certification

facilitate the verification process
key_tasks: Create a verification plan for a carbon project based on the verification scope, outlining objectives, criteria, timeline and resources required
Establish a data sampling methodology that ensures accuracy and reliability for verifying a carbon project
Plan the procedures for verifying data accuracy, data collection, monitoring and management practices, ensuring consistency with carbon standards

Review carbon projects as part of 
pre-verification assessment
key_tasks: Define the scope of verification, project timelines and the applicable carbon standards based on the specifications of the carbon project

Identify preliminary inconsistencies, missing data or areas that require clarification before on-site verification of a carbon project
Analyse potential risks, complexities and specific areas of concern within the carbon project that could impact verification

The Insurer for Decarbonisation Projects leads the underwriting of insurance policies, assesses and manages risks and claims for decarbonisation projects through risk and claims management processes. He/She works closely with other stakeholders, such as project developers, financial institutions, regulators, policy makers and civil society organisations to ensure the successful implementation and execution of insurance policies for decarbonisation projects in adherence to national and international reporting compliance frameworks. He reviews existing insurance portfolios to evaluate the evolving impact of climate change on insured assets. 

The Insurer for Decarbonisation Projects requires strong analytical and decision-making skills, as well as attention to detail. With in-depth knowledge of climate change, decarbonisation projects and their associated risks, he represents the company as a subject-matter expert in decarbonisation project insurance policies.

national and international reporting compliance frameworks
